reader.requirement: At --std 85, MOVE CORR identifier-3 TO identifier-4 must be accepted and behave exactly as MOVE CORRESPONDING identifier-3 TO identifier-4 (same pairs, same moves, same refusals), with CORR a reserved word.

edition-consulted.switches: whether CORR is reserved at an edition; the CORR row is reserved at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023

reader.edition-search: the moveStatement alternative (CORRESPONDING | CORR) and MoveBinder#Bind's test of both tokens carry no edition check (grep Edition/DialectLevel/ConstructRegistry near MoveBinder.cs line 155).
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1_move_corr_equivalence compares CORR and CORRESPONDING on one alphanumeric and one numeric pair; nested-group pairs, OCCURS exclusion, edited receivers, the shared refusal and CORR's reserved status are not exercised

probes.expected: MOVE CORR and MOVE CORRESPONDING give identical receivers: signed scaled to numeric-edited '- 12.5', alphanumeric padded 'XYZ  ', OCCURS items untouched '??', nested SUB.D 042

probes.printed: error COBOL1757 (operand 'E1' is an elementary item) for both the CORR and the CORRESPONDING statement
error COBOL0901: 'CORR' is a reserved word in COBOL-85
probes.expected: CORR is a reserved word at 85, not a user-defined word

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.19.3 SR2  (6.19.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2

reader.notes: The grammar spells the format-2 keyword as one choice (CORRESPONDING | CORR) and MoveBinder#Bind takes the same CorrespondingBinder path for either token, so the two spellings cannot diverge. Diagnostics cite §2023 clause numbers at --std 85 (wording only).

refuter.evidence: cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.6.19.3 SR2  the text is in SR2. Probes at --std 85: c1 MOVE CORR G OF R1 TO G OF R2 and MOVE CORRESPONDING G IN R1 TO G IN R3 (qualified, numeric to numeric-edited, alphanumeric padding, a same-named item under OCCURS and an unmatched item left out) printed identical receivers '[ 12ABC  ][ 12ABC  ]'; c2 MOVE CORR R1 TO R2 R3 (format 2 has a single identifier-2) refused COBOL0307; c3 MOVE CORR R1 TO R2(1:2) refused COBOL1757. The abbreviation reaches the one CORRESPONDING path; nothing CORR admits or refuses differs from the full word.
